newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Peru to sign accords during Fujimori's trip.
newsitem.headline: India, Peru to sign accords during Fujimori's trip.

text.p: India and Peru will sign six agreements during a four-day visit by President Alberto Fujimori next week, the Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday.
The agreements will strengthen ties between the two developing nations which have growing but modest trade relations, foreign ministry officials said.

Fujimori, on his first trip to South Asia, was set to arrive in the Indian capital from Dhaka on Sunday. He will spend Monday in New Delhi meeting Indian government and business leaders before travelling to Bombay on Tuesday.

The agreements will cover agricultural and technical cooperation, research in Antartica, tourism, consultations between the foreign offices and cooperation between the two nations' foreign service academies.
Last year India exported $41 million worth of goods to Peru, mainly motorcyles, bicycles, tyres and tubes, three-wheel vehicles, pharmaceuticals, auto and bicycle parts, textiles and rice.
India's imports from Peru, largely fishmeal, zinc and pima cotton, totalled $15 million.

"We want to exploit economic opportunities in Peru," Lalit Mansigh, a senior Foreign Ministry official, told reporters, saying the level of trade had increased dramatically in six years but did not reflect the potential.

The Foreign Ministry official said Fujimori's firm stand against guerrillas during the 127-day siege of the Japanese ambassador's residence was consistent with India's policy of refusing to yield to militants' demands.
"He stood firm, and we think his stand was vindicated," Mansingh said.
Peruvian troops killed 14 rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) during an April 22 operation to release their 72 hostages, who had been held at the residence since Dec. 17.
Two soldiers and one of the hostages also died in the bloody finale to the crisis.
